correspondence.component_scope: Selected mainstem FID 9281
correspondence.finding: Full ordinary corridor from the northwestern small-lake feeder setting to the southeastward mainstem fragment break, read in Hudon maps1–11 and their overlaps.

subcomponents.part: Northwestern feeder and initial lake connectors
observations: Map1 shows small headwater lakes linked by a narrow channel in the Route510 setting, followed by a longer lake and an eastward river corridor. The branch draining a larger lake north of the road is distinguished from the selected west-to-east route.

The selected headward course corresponds at generalized corridor scale to the northwestern feeder setting, the chain of small lake/channel transitions, the eastward bend, and then the southward elbow. The lakes are not given separate readable hydronyms; their names remain null.

Maps1–4 follow the same trunk through the eastward elbow into a long south-running valley, with short rapids, island splits and tributary entrances. Repeated Saint-Augustin labels occur on this connected corridor.

Side rivers and off-channel lakes remain separate, including tributaries entering the meandering reach and the larger west-side drainage toward the canyon. No disconnection or large selected reservoir passage is shown.

Map5 shows the main river turning through a steep canyon and receiving Michaels River from the western side at its lower end. Maps6–7 provide overlapping first-hand canyon annotations, while map8 carries the joined main river onward.

The field account distinguishes the main canyon from the portage to, and separate descent along, Michaels River. The selected mainstem follows the canyon and downstream joined trunk, rather than treating the portage as a water connector or renaming Michaels River.

subcomponents.part: Long southeastern valley and fragment transition
observations: Maps8–11 show the lower-canyon river widening, bending and then following the long southeastward valley with bars, islands and rapids. Map10 marks a distinct tributary Rivière Aux Saumons entering the main valley.

The selected route continues on Saint-Augustin through these tributary junctions and into the mapped bend system leading to the FID9282 continuation; the inventory fragment division is not a hydronym boundary.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected mainstem FID 9282
correspondence.finding: Full ordinary corridor from the inherited fragment break, through the southeast and south lower valley, to the selected rendered endpoint, read in maps11–17.
correspondence.correspondence: Full ordinary corridor from the inherited fragment break, through the southeast and south lower valley, to the selected rendered endpoint, read in maps11–17.

subcomponents.part: Southeastern bend and Rivière à la Mouche junction
observations: Maps11–12 show the main river changing from its long southeastward valley into the local eastward bend and south-running lower corridor. Islanded and rapid-bearing sections remain on the same mapped river.
Map13 explicitly shows Rivière à la Mouche joining Saint-Augustin as a distinct tributary. The selected line stays on the main river below that confluence.

subcomponents.part: Lower river with bends and bars
observations: Maps14–16 continue the trunk through the lower rapids, broad meander bends and then the wide sandy/barred south-flowing valley. Side lakes and short tributaries are mapped outside the main corridor.
The map depicts a wide lower river, not a chain of named lake interiors or a reservoir. The selected generalized line corresponds to this continuous main-valley setting.

subcomponents.part: Actual selected endpoint and downstream receiving setting
observations: Map17 and its printed grid place the selected rendered endpoint in the lower Saint-Augustin channel near the approach to the large western-branch junction, north of the Pakuashipi–Saint-Augustin settlement reach. The source-endpoint and rendered-endpoint metadata are distinct; neither is adopted as an exact open-sea mouth.

The same map continues downstream past the settlements through bars and islands into Baie de Saint-Augustin. Commission record55693 independently identifies Saint-Augustin Nord-Ouest as a lower tributary and places the named river outlet in the bay.
This downstream source context identifies the receiving system without extending the selected geometry into the bay or assuming uniform names for the bay and its channels.
subcomponents.map_locator: Map17, PDFpage4; CTQ Origine et signification

correspondence.component_scope: Selected southern start in the Upper Kesagami Lake setting
correspondence.finding: The retained P.3599-Revised original depicts and labels Upper Kesagami Lake in the selected southern headward setting. This is the beginning of the retained selection, not a claim to have identified the ultimate source of the named river. Several nearby small waterbodies, including separately labelled Little Kesagami Lake, are present.
correspondence.correspondence: Headward setting identified, but the complete exit and subsequent lake/channel chain are not confidently resolved in the overprinted original.
correspondence.name_observation: Upper Kesagami Lake is a map label for the headward waterbody. It does not label the subsequent entire channel. Little Kesagami Lake is kept as an adjacent/contextual label; traversal by the selection is not established.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwest-bending upper corridor and intermediate waterbody connectors south of the P.3757 map frame
correspondence.finding: The selected route bends northwest from the Upper Kesagami setting, then turns north/northeast toward the lakeward corridor. P.3599-Revised shows hydrographic linework, small lakes and the Cooks Pond and Lower Severn Lake labels in this regional corridor. Dense geological and geophysical overprinting prevents an adequately confident read of every selected lake entry, outlet and intermediate connection. The labels alone are not substituted for tracing those connections.
correspondence.correspondence: Material source-reading gap remains in the upper connector chain. This is not merely a naming-scope hold or an exact-bank/vertex discrepancy.
correspondence.name_observation: The selected channel and intermediate lake names remain null. Cooks Pond, Lower Severn Lake and Little Kesagami Lake are not assigned as a confirmed traversed sequence.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern lakeward channel and Newnham Bay
correspondence.finding: The P.3757 original covers the southern approach from its southern frame, showing the northward channel through a low-relief wetland landscape into the southern elongated Newnham Bay waterbody. The 1998 park map separately labels the incoming southern river Kesagami River. The inlet, elongated bay and northward water connection into the larger lake are visible at ordinary corridor scale.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported within the inspected P.3757 coverage; does not backfill the unresolved upper chain farther south.
correspondence.name_observation: Newnham Bay remains a separate named part of the lake passage. The park statement text spells this bay Newham in one passage; the inspected map/P.3757 spelling Newnham is retained.

correspondence.component_scope: Kesagami Lake passage, eastern basin and northeastern outlet
correspondence.finding: P.3757 and the 1998 park map show the elongated southern Newnham Bay connecting into Kesagami Lake. The selected generalized passage continues on the eastern side of the main lake, east of the Big Island setting, then toward the northeastern bay/outlet and the northbound river. Patawagamau Lake is a separately labelled narrow waterbody farther east in P.3757; its name is not transferred to the selected main-lake passage. The lake has islands, bays and adjacent smaller waterbodies rather than a uniformly named river reach.
correspondence.correspondence: Lake inlet, main-lake passage and northeastern river outlet supported at ordinary generalized corridor scale. No precise model-vertex/bank agreement or hydronym polygon boundary is asserted.
correspondence.name_observation: Kesagami Lake, Newnham Bay, and the separate adjacent Patawagamau Lake label are distinguished. No reservoir name or dam is established for this passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward and northeastward Kesagami River below the lake
correspondence.finding: The 1998 1:250,000 park-area map and retained P.3599-Revised original show the river leaving the northeastern lake outlet, following the northward corridor, then bending northeast/east toward the receiving-river junction. Tributaries enter from both sides; they are separate features, not a uniform extension of the representative name.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported for the mapped lower Kesagami corridor and receiving junction.
correspondence.name_observation: Kesagami River is directly labelled on the original park map and P.3599-Revised. The park statement describes the lake outlet to the Haarricanaw confluence; its published 112-kilometre figure describes that park/canoe-route scope and is not substituted for the inherited 216.850-kilometre model length.

correspondence.component_scope: Receiving-river junction and actual southern James Bay estuarine terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The selected route continues beyond the Kesagami receiving junction along the northward shared lower estuarine waterway to the southern James Bay inlet setting. The original 1998 park maps depict the junction and receiving outlet; page6 identifies the receiver as Haarricanaw River and places the confluence just south of Hannah Bay on James Bay. P.3599-Revised shows the broad receiving channel and coastal/inlet setting. The terminal is therefore accounted for as a shared estuarine receiver, not represented as a separately verified Kesagami-only sea mouth.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at broad component/corridor and actual terminal-setting scale; no precise legal mouth point or coastline vertex is claimed.
correspondence.name_observation: Haarricanaw River is the literal spelling in the inspected primary prose. The commonly used Harricana form is not relied on here as a newly verified registry name. Hannah Bay and James Bay are the supporting primary-prose terminal setting.
